To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the young broiler chicks fed diets that contain FCM at levels that provide as little as 75 mg of FB1/ kg of feed have increased free sphinganine and sphinganine/sphingosine levels, and that these levels are increased further as the FB1 concentration in feed is increased.

feeding broiler chicks diets containing Fusarium culture material that supplied 450 or 525 mg of fumonism B1 per kg of feed caused decreased feed intakes and growth, increased liver and kidney weights, and increased sphinganine levels in plasma and tissues.

feeding broiler chicks diets containing FCM, containing FB1 at levels as low as approximately 75 mg FB 1/kg, affects the physiology of the chick by increasing free sphangosine levels and sphingosine: sphingosine ratios, and that diets containing FCM containing FB1 at concentrations of 225 mg/kg or greater cause histological lesions in the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of feeding Fusarum moniliforme mycotoxin culture material on the young broilers.
the effects of feeding diets containing fumonisin to the young broiler.
the effects of feeding FCM containing known concentrations of FB1 in the diet to young broiler chickens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diets containing FCM, which supplied 75 mg FB/kg or higher, adversely affected the physiology and performance of broiler chicks.
the results from this experiment suggest that diets containing FCM, that supply levels as low as or higher than 75 mg FB 1/kg, may have adverse effects on the physiology of the young broiler.

feeding diets containing FCM to young broiler chick resulted in a dose-dependent increase in the incidence and severity of liver lesions, and that diets containing FCM, which supplied 225 mg or greater of FB1/kg, were toxic to young broilers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fumonisins have a negative effect on young broiler chicks at levels as low as the 75 mg/kg diet.
diets containing 225 mg FB 1/kg or more are toxic to the young broiler chicks, whereas diets containing 75 to 150 mg FB1/kg may be marginally toxic to the young chicks.
the toxicological effects of feeding F. moniliforme to young chicks are dependent on both the level of FB1 present in the culture and the age of the chicks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fumonisin mycotoxins are toxic at very low concentrations.
the effects of fumonisis on broiler chicks can be detected at levels of FB1 that are lower than those that produce overt toxicity in other species.
fumonisin mycotoxin can have adverse effects on young chicks at levels as low as about 75mg/kg.
